# Positive pair endpoints do not supply positive returns or a high-occupation pair sector

29 October 2026. New analytic construction; independent review pending. This is a scoped failure of direct paired-boundary renewal and of bare/near-identity paired truncation. It is NOT a sign-problem hardness theorem or a lower bound on arbitrary canonical, tensor, squeezed-state or correlated-field algorithms.

## 1. Native class and the exact positive endpoint operation

For M sites, fix K>=1 particles of EACH flavor and

`H=b†Tb+c†conjugate(T)c+U sum_i(nb_i-nc_i)^2`, `T>=0`, `U>0`.

All one-body diagonal terms are retained. The q_i^2 operator includes its normal-order linear number term. There is no occupation cutoff or pair-creation term. All fixed-number spaces are finite, with one-flavor dimension `D_(M,K)=binom(K+M-1,M-1)`.

Identify `|n>_b|m>_c` with the matrix unit `|n><m|` on the one-flavor K-particle space. If T_K=dGamma(T), H becomes the positive self-adjoint Hilbert--Schmidt superoperator

`Hcal(A)=T_K A+A T_K+U sum_i[n_i,[n_i,A]]`.             (1)

The map Phi_t=exp(-t Hcal) is completely positive and trace nonincreasing: dephasing is trace preserving, and the other factor is A->exp(-sT_K)A exp(-sT_K) with T_K>=0. Finite-dimensional product convergence suffices. The finite-slice HS formula has Kraus operators Gamma_K(B), and therefore

`F_nm(t)=<n,n|exp(-tH)|m,m>`

`= <n|Phi_t(|m><m|)|n> >=0`.                          (2)

At finite slices it is exactly the Gaussian average of `|<n|Gamma_K(B)|m>|^2`; the finite-K limit preserves positivity. Each column of F has sum at most one. This is a genuine positive endpoint operation, not a claim that its individual permanent amplitudes are supplied efficiently.

They are different. In the matrix picture Z is the superoperator trace over ALL matrix units, not the trace restricted to diagonal matrix units or a sum of population transition probabilities. A preparation/dressing or discarded-weight theorem is required before using Z_P as Z.

29 October 2026. Analytic construction completed; independent review pending. Governing arguments are in [PROOF.md](PROOF.md). No new many-body sampling or physical measurement is claimed.

Positive paired imaginary-time endpoints are exact for the native conjugate-flavor model. They do not, however, supply positive first-return weights or the full critical Gibbs trace.

**Positive-return failure on a genuine many-mode family.** Repeat the accepted frustrated trimer and connect neighboring blocks by fixed rational PSD bonds. For EVERY M its exact paired Schur operator at U=1 has S12>1/10 and S13,S23<-2. Thus its exact first-return integral has a negative off-diagonal entry despite every endpoint being nonnegative. A diagonal phase change cannot remove the triangle sign.

# Direct critical sectors through paired endpoints

29 October 2026. Work begun after the normal-fluid/critical-number proofs froze.

The attempted operation is a direct canonical, interacting pair description, avoiding the proved normalizable-grand count filter. In the conjugate-flavor sector the Hamiltonian vectorizes to the trace-decreasing CP generator

`Hcal(A)=T_K A+A T_K+sum_i U_i[n_i,[n_i,A]]`.

Its diagonal-to-diagonal imaginary-time endpoints are nonnegative. The missing constructive step is whether the eliminated off-diagonal excursions have nonnegative, computable first-return weights. Positivity at endpoints does not acquire those weights or a permanent/Gibbs-element oracle.

The analytic discriminator is the exact Schur/Volterra memory, not another Monte Carlo sign test. A fixed native frustrated trimer gives a negative OFF-DIAGONAL integrated return weight. I will test whether the failure persists on an acquired connected, bounded-range, arbitrarily many-mode family and at arbitrary finite U, and whether the bare paired space even retains the high-occupation critical Gibbs mass. A negative result here would exclude a specific positive-renewal/pair-elimination construction, not arbitrary canonical algorithms.

The equally informed alternatives include canonical ED, correlated AFQMC, number-conserving Bogoliubov/squeezed states, strong-coupling pair/rotor models and tensor methods. Kuklov--Prokof'ev--Svistunov 2003 already derives pair Hamiltonians and performs loop-current Monte Carlo. Feshbach/Nakajima--Zwanzig elimination and Schrieffer--Wolff effective Hamiltonians are established machinery. Their approximation ranges, occupations and physical interactions must be matched; a second-order pair hopping term is not a newly acquired exact positive operator.

No Gibbs matrix-element oracle, permanent oracle, mixing gap, microscopic cutoff or spectral gap beyond what is actually derived is supplied.
